question: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 40 cm and the distance of Q from the centres is 41 cm. The radius of the circle is _______ cm.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius, the tangent, and the line joining the center to the external point form a **right-angled triangle**.

Using the common **Pythagorean triplet** (9, 40, 41):

Radius² + Tangent² = Distance²

r² + 40² = 41²

r² = 1681 − 1600 = 81

r = √81 = 9 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **tangent** (QT) = 40 cm

Distance of point Q from the **center** (OQ) = 41 cm

**Formula used:**

In a circle, the tangent at any point is **perpendicular** to the radius through the point of contact. By **Pythagoras Theorem**: Radius² + Tangent² = (Distance from center)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf1f7085e3c0309b8a4540db4ba370817a85a0d44dece4bfbf8821e1b547820b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **O** be the center of the circle and **T** be the point of contact of the tangent from **Q**.

⇒ In right-angled Δ**OTQ**, ∠**OTQ** = 90°.

⇒ OT² + QT² = OQ²

⇒ r² + 40² = 41²

⇒ r² + 1600 = 1681

⇒ r² = 1681 − 1600

⇒ r² = 81

⇒ r = √81 = 9 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

The radius of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, forming a 90° angle.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (9, 40, 41).

Length of Tangent

The length of a tangent from an external point is calculated as L = √(d² − r²), where d is the distance from the center and r is the radius.</p
